The elections took place alongside the rest of the [[2026 London local elections|local elections in London boroughs]]. It was part of the [[2026 United Kingdom local elections]]. ==Background== ===History=== The thirty-two [[London boroughs]] were established in 1965 by the [[London Government Act 1963]]. They are the principal authorities in Greater London and have responsibilities including education, housing, planning, highways, social services, libraries, recreation, waste, environmental health and revenue collection. Some of the powers are shared with the [[Greater London Authority]], which also manages passenger transport, police and fire.{{Cite web|title=The essential guide to London local government {{!}} London Councils|url=https://www.londoncouncils.gov.uk/who-runs-london/essential-guide-london-local-government|access-date=2021-10-10|website=www.londoncouncils.gov.uk}} === Council term === Following the 2022 election, the Conservatives were the largest group on the council but five seats short of a majority. The Havering Residents Association (HRA) entered into a leadership coalition with the [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]], with Ray Morgon (HRA, [[Hacton (ward)|Hacton]]) as council leader.{{cite news |title='Local parties running things is better': Ray Morgon on leading council |url=https://www.romfordrecorder.co.uk/news/24628725.ray-morgon-discusses-leading-havering-council-interview/ |access-date=4 February 2026 |work=Romford Recorder |date=6 October 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251010000640/https://www.romfordrecorder.co.uk/news/24628725.ray-morgon-discusses-leading-havering-council-interview/ |archive-date=10 October 2025 |language=en |url-status=live}} John Tyler (HRA, [[Cranham (ward)|Cranham]]) did not join the HRA group and sat as an independent.{{cite news |last1=Lynch |first1=Ben |title=Councillor leaves HRA group on council over Labour agreement |url=https://www.romfordrecorder.co.uk/news/20708604.councillor-leaves-hra-group-council-labour-agreement/ |access-date=30 December 2025 |work=Romford Recorder |date=24 June 2022 |language=en}} The [[Harold Wood Hill Park Residents Association]], who were no longer affiliated with the HRA, formed the three-member East Havering Residents Group. Following the July 2022 [[Wennington wildfire]], in September 2022, Sarah Edwards, Sue Ospreay and Jackie McArdle (all Conservative, [[Rainham and Wennington (ward)|Rainham and Wennington]]) defected to the HRA.{{cite news |last1=Mellor |first1=Josh |title=Tory trio defect to Havering Residents Association |url=https://www.yellowad.co.uk/tory-trio-defect-to-havering-residents-association/ |access-date=30 December 2025 |work=Yellow Advertiser |date=9 September 2022}} The May 2023 death of Linda Hawthorn (HRA, [[Upminster (ward)|Upminster]]) led to the [[2023 Upminster by-election]] and the election of Jacqueline Williams (also HRA).{{cite news |last1=Hayes |first1=George |title=Tributes to 'dedicated' Upminster councillor Linda Hawthorn |url=https://www.romfordrecorder.co.uk/news/23539027.tributes-dedicated-upminster-councillor-linda-hawthorn/ |access-date=30 December 2025 |work=Romford Recorder |date=22 May 2023 |language=en}}{{cite web |title=Local Elections Archive Project — Upminster Ward |url=https://www.andrewteale.me.uk/leap/ward/22342/#2023-08-10 |website=www.andrewteale.me.uk |access-date=30 December 2025}} In February 2024, Robby Misir (Conservative, [[Marshalls and Rise Park (ward)|Marshalls and Rise Park]]) joined the HRA and Philip Ruck (HRA, [[Cranham (ward)|Cranham]]) left the party to sit as an independent.{{cite web |last1=Boothroyd |first1=David |title=Quartet of change |url=https://www.localcouncils.co.uk/2024/02/quartet-of-change/ |website=localcouncils.co.uk |access-date=30 December 2025}} John Tyler and Philip Ruck then formed the two-member Residents Association Independent Group. Each ward returns either two or three councillors. Polling will take place on 7 May 2026.{{cite web |last1=Blake-Herbert |first1=Andrew |title=Notice of Election: Havering |url=https://drive.google.com/file/d/1OcvQAZ5bSQ3V-VOEGmSxgWNIs9ZmQhBn/view |website=Google Drive |publisher=Havering London Borough Council |access-date=10 April 2026 |language=en |format=PDF |date=26 March 2026 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260410102752/https://drive.google.com/file/d/1OcvQAZ5bSQ3V-VOEGmSxgWNIs9ZmQhBn/view |archive-date=10 April 2026 }}{{cite web |last1=Blake-Herbert |first1=Andrew |title=Notices of election agents' names and offices |url=https://drive.google.com/file/d/1J-08eLaJFUUO8Ngm5PQbunH5dUbCTku7/view |website=Google Drive |publisher=Havering London Borough Council |access-date=10 April 2026 |language=en |format=PDF |date=9 April 2026|url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260410103118/https://drive.google.com/file/d/1J-08eLaJFUUO8Ngm5PQbunH5dUbCTku7/view |archive-date=10 April 2026 }}{{Cite web|url=https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/election-timetable-in-england/election-timetable-in-england|title=Local authority, combined authority, and county combined authority election cycles in England|website=GOV.UK|accessdate=Nov 28, 2025}}{{cite web |last1=Blake-Herbert |first1=Andrew |title=Statement of Persons Nominated, Notice of Poll and Situation of Polling Stations |url=https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Thd0VCUh6H0H28qAOVmUiezhlXIikyYP/view |website=Google Drive |publisher=Havering London Borough Council |access-date=10 April 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260410150121/https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Thd0VCUh6H0H28qAOVmUiezhlXIikyYP/view |archive-date=10 April 2026 |format=PDF |date=10 April 2026 |url-status=live}} Havering, as is the case for all London borough councils, elects all of its councillors at once every four years, with the previous election having taken place in 2022. The election will take place by multi-member [[first-past-the-post voting]], with each ward being represented by two or three councillors. Electors will have as many votes as there are councillors to be elected in their ward, with the top two or three being elected. All [[Elections in the United Kingdom#Registration procedure|registered electors]] ([[British citizen|British]], [[Irish citizen|Irish]], [[Commonwealth citizen|Commonwealth]] and [[European Union]] citizens) living in London aged 18 or over will be entitled to vote in the election. People who live at two addresses in different councils, such as university students with different term-time and holiday addresses, are entitled to be registered for and vote in elections in both local authorities.{{Cite web|title=How the elections work {{!}} London Councils|url=https://www.londoncouncils.gov.uk/who-runs-london/london-elections/how-elections-work|access-date=2021-09-14|website=www.londoncouncils.gov.uk}} Voting in-person at polling stations will take place from 7:00 to 22:00 on election day, and voters will be able to apply for postal votes or proxy votes in advance of the election. == Previous council composition == [[File:Havering UK local
